prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1008; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of a northbound roadway in Houston, Texas, waiting for traffic to clear, when the vehicle directly behind, operated by Driver 2, struck the rear of Driver 1's car. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy involved, and the responding officer confirmed Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel at the scene. A Passenger was also present in the vehicle. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash, and the officer noted that the reported symptoms fit the type and force of a rear impact of this kind. The rear bumper and trunk area of Driver 1's vehicle showed damage that lines up with the described collision, and no earlier damage to the vehicle was known to the officer or to Driver 1. Scene photographs confirm several details of the impact and positions of both vehicles. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the statements of the drivers and the physical evidence at the scene. Both vehicles were moved to the shoulder, and traffic was directed around the area until the scene was cleared.
